samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the picture graph. How many are in dogs?
Look at the picture graph. How many are in grapes?
Look at the picture graph. How many are in roses?
Look at the picture graph. How many are in Monday?
Look at the picture graph. How many are in dogs?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The instruction 'Look at the picture graph. How many are in dogs?' with a lettered MCQ answer directly requires reading a count off an unscaled pictograph, which is exactly the 'interpret a pictograph without a scale' verb.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All five samples ask only the single question form 'How many are in [category]?'; no sample asks a comparison sub-case such as which category has the most or how many more one category has than another, so only the simplest read-a-count interpretation is exercised.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Each stem is a two-sentence, under-ten-word prompt, e.g. seed 43's 'Look at the picture graph. How many are in grapes?', matching Grade 1 Quarter 3 single-step reading demand.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The five samples reuse the identical template 'Look at the picture graph. How many are in [category]?' word-for-word every time, including seeds 42 and 46 both querying dogs, so no alternate question framing is exercised anywhere in the sample set.

competency_alignment.rationale: Distractors stay close to the keyed count, e.g. seed 45's options 9, 7 (correct), 6, 8 for Monday, which exercises careful pictograph reading rather than an unrelated computation or vocabulary skill.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Keyed counts across the five seeds range from 1 (seed 46's dogs) to 9 (seed 44's roses), staying within the small, scale-free range appropriate to a Grade 1 Quarter 3 pictograph.
